clauses.reason: Section 1 revokes the target order effective at noon on January 20, 2021 and adds that employees and former employees subject to its commitments will not be subject to them after that time. The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective time; once noon on January 20, 2021 passed it had nothing further to command. The date is the stated effective date, so no signing-date inference is needed (signed January 19, 2021). Quoted words: "is hereby revoked, effective" and "at noon January 20, 2021. Employees and former employees subject to the". Actor: the order itself; no later act was needed. The surviving consequence, that the target order stays revoked, is recorded under savings.

This general provision says nothing in the order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the matters in its items (i) and (ii); it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2021-01-20 (noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states).

Item (i) of the non-derogation provision preserves the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2021-01-20 (noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states).

Item (ii) of the non-derogation provision preserves the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2021-01-20 (noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states).

This general provision says the order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations; it conditions how the order is carried out. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2021-01-20 (noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states).

This general provision states that the order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit enforceable at law or in equity against the United States or others; it states the order's effect. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2021-01-20 (noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states).

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 13983, 86 FR 6835 (Federal Register Vol. 86, No. 14, Monday, January 25, 2021; filed January 22, 2021), signed January 19, 2021 (grade official_original_counted, machine text layer of the official PDF). The heading, number, title (Revocation of Executive Order 13770) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text; it is section 1 (revocation) and section 2 (general provisions), and the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the only operative command is the revocation of Executive Order 13770 of January 28, 2017 (Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees). It is a one-time act that was complete at noon on January 20, 2021, the effective time the order states, so section 1 and the clauses that operate alongside it end on 2021-01-20. No later instrument names this order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text and the dossier's later-event chain is empty.
